explanation: Bananas are rich in potassium, and a tiny share of all natural potassium is radioactive potassium-40. The dose from eating one is far too small to matter.

claims.text: Bananas are slightly radioactive because they contain potassium, which includes a small share of radioactive potassium-40.
About 0.012% of natural potassium is the radioactive isotope potassium-40.
The radiation dose from eating a banana is far too small to harm health.

Bananas are a well-known source of potassium, roughly 350 to 400 mg per 100 g.
Natural potassium contains 0.0117% potassium-40, which is radioactive, and bananas are rich in potassium, so a banana is faintly radioactive (roughly 15 becquerels).
